task_instance: Respond to a suspected Intercom outage (conversation sync failing / messages not sending): run the runbook's triage to produce a fault verdict (is it us or Intercom?), classify severity, apply the matching mitigation, and write the postmortem with captured Intercom request_ids.
blocker_detail: The skill's core deliverable is a fault verdict that must be backed by the triage script's live HTTP status codes, the platform status-page state, and the rate-limit response headers, followed by mitigation. Producing any of this requires executing shell commands the office-assistant runtime does not grant: the triage probes run curl plus jq against the Intercom REST API and status/incidents endpoints and inspect response headers; mitigation runs kubectl rollout restart and an AWS secrets-manager token rotation. This runtime cannot run code or commands of any kind. Secondary blockers also apply: no Intercom workspace admin access token is available (and must not be sought), and the target endpoints are unreachable placeholders while web access is disallowed this round. The only text-only artifacts (Slack update, postmortem) cannot be genuinely completed because the runbook requires them to carry the real HTTP codes and captured Intercom request_ids from the triage run, and fabricating that tool-returned data is not permitted.
evidence: Read SKILL.md and all three reference files (references/triage.md, mitigation.md, templates.md) at the skill path. The triage 'Quick Triage' script is a bash script invoking curl + jq against the Intercom API, status endpoint, incidents endpoint, and a local health check, plus a curl header grep for the rate-limit remaining value; the decision tree branches on the returned HTTP status (401/403/429/5xx). Mitigation reference uses aws secretsmanager and kubectl rollout restart. Created a sample incident input at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/b273891e-4b73-5af7-9840-fc512af93809/scratchpad/real2_work/r195/incident_alert.md to drive a concrete instance, then reached the first runbook step (the triage probe) and stopped: the probe cannot be executed because this runtime runs no shell/code (curl/jq/kubectl/aws unavailable), there is no access token, and endpoints are unreachable placeholders. No deliverable produced or verified.
